searchText: Hi all, do we have a report (besides prismatic's one) that provides data and timings about the crash of last weekend? something like at time xx:xx this client started to be out of sync.. time xx:xx a new version is released time xx:xx this many nodes restart time xx:xx this number of nodes are out... etc etc the idea would be to be able to replay this in a simulation Unfortunately a lot of it happened over the weekend, so not everything was tracked as closely. Prysmatic has a system set up to track incidents like this though, so maybe they have such data. Another problem is that clients prune away non-finalized chains, so reconstructing the whole event will be quite difficult I see, that is unfortunate And although we're now building something to monitor the network more closely, at the time we didn't monitor extensively beyond eth2stats, and our own nodes. And each node has their own point of view, with different forks, due to the following sync problems after the event. So it's hard to say exactly how many nodes went out, and which forks were made. Currently building some infra to manage multiple rumor instances better, and have them crawl + collect gossip data next. It already has functionality to aggregate and tee peerstore changes, poll status/metadata, etc. Maybe next time there's something interesting on the net, we can replay it. good, do you have a link to this monitoring tool? or is it just rumor plus some few scripts on top of it? rumor is open source, `peerstore create` and `peer track ...` commands may be what you are looking for. we will take a look at it For orchestrating more rumor instances, and merging their work, I'm more hesitant to make it open source, as it's more of a devops thing than a programming thing, and exposes the network to more than just friendly crawling we are writing a small user guide on rumor, similar to what you did https://github.com/leobago/BSC-ETH2/tree/master/rumor If anything, we'll harden the spec against any attacks we come up with. And anyone is welcome to try and use rumor to strike up some attacknet bounty Great 👏 so we will be documenting on those functions as well The other guide, if anyone can't find the link anymore: https://notes.ethereum.org/@protolambda/rumor-tutorial The peerstore tracking is relatively new, don't have that in my own tutorial just yet, but it's there ok, we will explore that and document it we could do a merge later The idea is relatively simple though: - create 1 peerstore - create N hosts, using the same peerstore - make the hosts crawl the network, with the many p2p commands in there, including some specifically for polling - peerstore is updated like in any normal libp2p app - peerstore changes are tee'd: like the common linux tool, just pipe the same changes to a log, with support for different formats, and soon streaming to external server And the evcsv/evjson formats translate the peerstore structure into something more readable and structured, for easier processing. Anywaay, I'll open up a channel for tooling/datascience, and then we don't spam this channel too much. Sorry everyone 😅 awesome, thanks <@!203220829473996800> ! <#746343380900118528> is now open! And we'll open up some challenges for data-science in Eth2 soon, stay tuned 🙂 one tool we have is `ncli_db` that can take a nimbus database and extract states/blocks from it, as well as replay the entire block history - this is pretty useful on something like medalla because the non-finalized period is stored in the database as well added to the tooling list doc. See <#746343380900118528> for more tooling discussion

The idea is relatively simple though:
- create 1 peerstore
- create N hosts, using the same peerstore
- make the hosts crawl the network, with the many p2p commands in there, including some specifically for polling
- peerstore is updated like in any normal libp2p app
- peerstore changes are tee'd: like the common linux tool, just pipe the same changes to a log, with support for different formats, and soon streaming to external server

excerpts.author: protolambda
